name: MathDial
summary: About 2,900 one-to-one tutoring dialogues in which teachers tutor a simulated student through a mistaken solution to a math word problem, annotated with the teachers' moves.

license.note: The GitHub README says CC BY-SA 4.0 and the Hugging Face card CC BY 4.0; there is no LICENSE file. The students' turns are written by a model.

cite: Macina, J., Daheim, N., Chowdhury, S. P., Sinha, T., Kapur, M., Gurevych, I., & Sachan, M. (2023). MathDial: A Dialogue Tutoring Dataset with Rich Pedagogical Properties Grounded in Math Reasoning Problems. Findings of EMNLP 2023. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2023.findings-emnlp.372

fits.how: A mistaken solution becomes a test case, with what the teacher saw in it. Its students also hold a mistake through a whole dialogue, a pattern for a simulated learner, which agent tests don't use yet.

connect.note: A learner shows a mistaken solution: does the reply find the mistake with a question or a hint, without giving the answer? The solutions are written by a model; the teachers who read them are real. It shows what your judge read in these replies, not what learners learn. Asks you to accept its license first.
